prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single “audit” that tells you whether ChatGPT (or other LLMs) will recommend your business. The best practical approach is a two-part strategy: (A) make sure your business appears reliably in the data sources LLMs use (local listings, knowledge graph, structured data), and (B) actively test LLMs by querying them. For most small businesses the best single tool to manage and monitor presence is a local-listings service such as BrightLocal or Yext — combined with occasional direct queries to ChatGPT/other models via their web UIs or APIs.

What to do and what tools to use

1) Ensure the data sources LLMs read from are correct
- Claim and optimize your Google Business Profile (GBP). This is critical.
- Claim Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Yelp, TripAdvisor and any major industry directories.
- Add structured data (schema.org LocalBusiness) to your website and keep NAP (name, address, phone) consistent.
Tools: Yext, BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark, Semrush Local (these help create and monitor listings across directories).

2) Monitor reviews and reputation
- LLMs often surface highly rated businesses. Monitor reviews on Google, Yelp, Facebook.
Tools: BrightLocal, BirdEye, ReviewTrackers, Podium.

3) Check search presence and knowledge panel
- Use Google Search Console and the Google Knowledge Panel to see how Google represents you (often LLMs consult the same web content and knowledge graphs).

4) Test LLMs directly
- Ask the models themselves (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Bard, Anthropic Claude). You can do this manually via the web UI or automate via APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Cloud Generative AI).
- Example prompts to test:
  - “Recommend good [business type] options in [city], especially those with [feature].”
  - “What are the top-rated [business type] near [address or ZIP]?”
  - “If I need [service X] in [city], who should I call?”
- Vary phrasing and location context. If your business appears, copy the reply and note sources (if shown).

5) Automate/monitor over time
- For continuous checks, script queries using OpenAI / Anthropic / Google APIs and log whether your business appears in the replies.
- Combine that with listing-monitoring tools (BrightLocal / Yext) so you’re alerted if a directory listing breaks.

Which single “best” service?
- For a small business that wants a simple all-in-one solution: BrightLocal is widely used and cost-effective for local SEO, listing consistency, rank/review monitoring and reporting.
- If you have more budget and want enterprise-level control over directory data, Yext is strong at pushing authoritative structured data to many platforms (which helps downstream consumers and models).
- For checking AI responses specifically, there’s no dedicated “AI recommendation monitor” product yet — you’ll need to query models directly (via ChatGPT or the OpenAI API, or the equivalent APIs for Bing/Google/Anthropic).

Quick action plan (3 steps)
1. Claim Google Business Profile and other major listings; add schema.org markup to your website.
2. Sign up for BrightLocal (or Yext) to manage and monitor listings and reviews.
3. Manually test ChatGPT/Bing/Bard with sample prompts and/or set up periodic automated API checks.

If you want, tell me your business type and city and I’ll draft a few specific test prompts and a short checklist you can use in BrightLocal or a small API script to monitor LLM recommendations.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
